page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. Built upon the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Hardware cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache. It incorporates instruction set extensions such as AVX, AVX-512F, FMA, and AES.

System memory totals 64.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio at 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent disk operations. There are no dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs configured. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are allocated.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear contrast between single-threaded execution and aggregate parallel throughput. Single-core evaluations reflect lower-tier performance, with stress-ng single-core reaching 1107.49 and Geekbench single-core reaching 963.0. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics fall consistently in the middle tier, supported by a stress-ng multi-core score of 23528.93, a Geekbench multi-core score of 8384.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 23057.96. In-memory and caching metrics demonstrate stable capabilities, logging 23.22 million Redis SET operations per second and 13.98 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the ecs.sn1ne.8xlarge is optimized for workloads that prioritize parallel execution across 32 dedicated threads over raw per-core clock speed. Because single-thread execution is relatively modest, the instance is best matched with distributed tasks, multi-threaded batch operations, Clang software builds, web serving fleets, and background ETL processing.

The instance features no local storage, lacks dedicated GPUs, and supplies a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. Empirical benchmark testing reveals moderate multi-core throughput, reflected in a PassMark CPU score of 23057.96 and multi-core Geekbench score of 8384.0, contrasted with lower single-core execution speeds in stress-ng and Geekbench. Memory bandwidth benchmarks place in the middle 50%, alongside stable web serving and caching capabilities, achieving 23.22 million Redis SET operations per second. It is suited for parallel compute tasks, CI/CD compilation, distributed web services, and batch data processing workloads that do not require high per-core single-thread throughput.
